sentences.text: Date : 07.03.2025 Heard Mr. I. Hussain, learned counsel for the petitioner; Ms. R. Bora, learned Standing Counsel, NHIDCL for the respondent nos. 1, 2 & 5; and Ms. S. Baruah, learned Junior Government Advocate, Assam for the respondent nos. 3, 4 & 6.
Page No.# 3/4 2.

The petitioner has claimed that he is in occupation of a plot of land, covered by Dag no. 194, at Ochaman Ali vs The Union Of India And 7 Ors on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30434367/
2 Revenue Village - Gotaimari, Mouza - Silabandha, Naduar Revenue Circle, District - Sonitpur, by constructing a dwelling house with kitchen & toilet, etc. and also by growing trees on the plot.

sentences.text: The plot of land is a Government land.
The respondent authorities have, in the meantime, initiated a process of land acquisition in order to construct a guide bundh to prevent 4-lane National Highways from flood waters.

The case projected by the petitioner is that in the process of land acquisition, the petitioner's dwelling house, toilet, kitchen, plantations, etc. on the said plot of land were surveyed for assessment but his name was not included in the final list of beneficiaries.
The petitioner has stated that he submitted a number of representations before the respondent authorities but the same did not elicit any response.
Hence the writ petition.

3. Ms. Baruah, learned Junior Government Advocate who was asked to obtain instructions from the respondent no. 3 on the previous date, 24.02.2025, has placed an Office Letter no. E-140922/117 dated 05.03.2025 of the respondent no. 3, addressed to the office of the Government Advocate,
Gauhati High Court.

4. As per the Office Letter dated 05.03.2025, it is mentioned, contrary to the claim of the petitioner that the Dag no. 194 in Village no. 1 Gataimari has been acquired by the respondent authorities for the purpose of construction of Guide Bund, that the land within Dag no. 194 did not fall inside the Right of Way of the Guide Bund and hence, it was not enlisted either of the notifications, issued Page No.# 4/4 under Section 3A, Section 3D and Section 3G of the National Highways Act, 1956.
With such projections, the respondent no. 3 has mentioned that the issue of payment of compensation to the petitioner does not arise.
5. The matter would require further consideration.

6. Issue notice, returnable on 07.04.2025.
7.

As Ms. Bora, learned Standing Counsel, NHIDCL has appeared and accepted notice on behalf of the respondent nos. 1, 2 & 5 and Ms. Barua, learned Junior Government Advocate has appeared and accepted notice on behalf of the respondent nos. 3, 4 & 6, no formal notices need to be issued to the respondents.

Mr. Hussain, learned counsel for the petitioner shall furnish requisite nos. of extra copies of the writ petitions along with the annexures to Ms. Bora and Ms. Barua within 2 [two]
working days from today.
8. The respondents shall bring their stands in their respective counter affidavits on or before the returnable date.
9. A copy of the Office Letter no. E-140922/117 dated 05.03.2025 is to be kept with the case record.
